name: Piz Buin

lead: Piz Buin is a European sun care brand used for holiday and outdoor sun protection and a steadier, less burnt tan. Less sunburn and sun damage means more even, healthier-looking skin.

It traces to Franz Greiter's 1946 Gletscher Crème and is named after an Alpine mountain. Sunscreen filters as a class are well studied; for the brand itself, published use is limited to old 1980s mouse experiments.

paras: People apply it to exposed skin before sun exposure and reapply through the day, choosing the SPF to suit their skin type. It is used on holidays and for outdoor sport, and some pair it with after-sun care.
Sunscreen lowers but does not eliminate sunburn and UV damage, and it works only as long as it is applied generously and reapplied. No human studies of the brand were found.

angle.text: Piz Buin is a European sun care brand, descended from a 1946 glacier cream, used for outdoor sun protection and a steadier tan. UV filters in the cream cut burning and sun damage, which keeps skin tone more even and healthy-looking.

lead: Piz Buin is a European sun care brand. According to Wikipedia, Austrian chemist Franz Greiter introduced a product called Gletscher Crème in 1946 that became the basis for Piz Buin, named after the mountain where Greiter reportedly got sunburned [1].
Published scientific use of the brand is limited to old animal experiments in which it served as a test sunscreen.

paras: Greiter's 1946 glacier cream was the basis for the brand [1]. Wikipedia credits the name to the mountain where he allegedly suffered sunburn [1].

No studies found in humans. Animal studies exist: a 1984 hairless-mouse study used a commercial sunscreen to compare protection against vascular injury and epidermal cell damage [2], and a 1985 study of long-term UV exposure of mouse eyes included a group protected with a Piz Buin factor 6 lotion alongside one using a factor 5 product and an unprotected group [3].
